symptom: A long-running self-maintenance scheduler can repeatedly spend a subprocess startup importing apscheduler and pytest for an unchanged focused-test interpreter; a path-only successful-result cache would then keep selecting an interpreter after it is deleted, replaced, made non-executable, or loses dependencies.
root_cause: Focused-test interpreter suitability is a time-varying property, but the prior caching approach bound a successful dependency probe only to the candidate path and returned the cached result before revalidating file identity, execute permission, and probe freshness.

executable_template.applicability_check: Call _python_supports_focused_tests repeatedly for one candidate, confirm unchanged calls repeat the dependency subprocess, then model a cached success followed by chmod, deletion, same-path replacement, or a dependency probe failure after cache expiry.
executable_template.patch_strategy: Cache the dependency probe for at most 30 seconds and eight candidates, key reuse by executable stat identity, recheck file existence and execute permission before every cache hit, evict invalid candidates immediately, and re-run the real import probe when identity changes or freshness expires.
executable_template.rollback_plan: Revert the bounded cache, executable fingerprint helper, and cache invalidation regressions together; retain uncached probing until another design proves both current executability and dependency availability before emitting the focused-test command.
